sentences.text: ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through PP

----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Vineet Jain, Sr. Adv.
 Mr. Khet Singh Rajpurohit

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sharwan Singh, PP  Mr. M.S. Purohit &
 Mr. Amit Kumar Purohit for  complainant  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 08/11/2024 1. This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. (483 BNSS) has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.262/2024, registered at Police Station Sridungargarh, District Bikaner, for offences under Sections 307, 341, 323, 354, 376(2)(n), 382, 384 and 506 of IPC.
2.

As per the prosecution, the allegation against the present petitioner is of subjecting prosecutrix to forcible sexual assault- rape on multiple occasions by threatening her to viral her obscene videos and photographs.

Further, an allegation has also been levelled against the petitioner that when the prosecutrix, being bothered and harassed by the acts of the petitioner, returned to her village Toliasar, the petitioner on on 02.05.2024, forcibly [2024:RJ-JD:45158] (2 of 5)
[CRLMB-10893/2024] entered her house at Toliasar and tried to obtain her signatures on a letter.
The petitioner also molested her at knife point.

sentences.text: 3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned counsels for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Drawing attention of the Court towards the FIR as well as the challan papers, learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix is a mature lady aged about 30 years.

Learned counsel submitted that the material available on record prima facie indicates that while living in Punjab, the prosecutrix developed consensual physical relationship with the present petitioner in the year 2023.

However, on relations between them turning strained, the petitioner has been roped in a false criminal case.
5.

Learned counsel vehemently submitted that neither the obscene videos and photographs allegedly captured by the petitioner to blackmail and threaten the prosecutrix have been recovered nor he has been chargesheeted for the offences under the Information Technology Act.
It was contended that even the letter upon which the petitioner allegedly tried to obtain the signatures of the prosecutrix has not been handed over by her to the police.

She has also not provided the recording of the telephonic conversations which have taken place between her and the petitioner on a number of occasions to substantiate the contention that the relationship between them was not mutual.

[2024:RJ-JD:45158] (3 of 5) [CRLMB-10893/2024]
6. Drawing attention of the Court towards the challan papers, learned counsel submitted that the petitioner has also been chargesheeted for the offences under Section 307 IPC on the count that the petitioner who was keeping animosity with the husband of the petitioner, had caused him grievous head injuries whereas the medical reports of the husband of the prosecutrix indicate that he had received the aforementioned head injuries due to a roadside accident.

7. Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioner.
8. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned counsels for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application.

Learned counsels for the complainant submitted that the statements of the prosecutrix and the other witnesses are sufficient to establish that the relationship between the two was not consensual and the prosecutrix was subjected to forcible sexual assault- rape by the petitioner on multiple occassions.

9. Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that as per the prosecutrix, she was subjected to forcible sexual assault - rape for the first time on 03.12.2023.
Thereafter, by threatening her to circulate her obscene photos and videographs on multiple occasions, the petitioner committed rape upon her.
As per the prosecutrix on 02.05.2024, the petitioner forcibly entered her house and tried to obtain her signatures on a letter.

On a careful [2024:RJ-JD:45158] (4 of 5) [CRLMB-10893/2024] scanning of the material available on record, this Court finds that no obscene videos or photographs of the prosecutrix have been recovered by the Investigating Agency; the petitioner has not even been chargesheeted for the Gordhan Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45158) on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179275311/

entities.text: Gordhan Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45158)

sentences.text: 2 offences under the Information Technology Act; neither the letter on which petitioner tried to obtain the signatures of the prosecutrix nor the allegedly recorded telephonic conversations between the two have been handed over to the Investigating Agency by the complainant.

10. Upon a perusal of the medical reports annexed with the record, this Court further finds that K.D.
Ganesha Hospital, Amritsar, while discharging the husband of the petitioner from hospital on 07.04.2024 has recorded the cause of injuries sustained by him to be roadside accident.
It is also to be noticed that no separate FIR with regard to the petitioner having inflicted injuries upon the husband of the prosecutrix at the relevant time was lodged.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
11. Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. (483 BNSS) is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Gordhan Singh S/o Rameshwar Lal arrested in connection with F.I.R.
No.262/2024, registered at Police Station Sridungargarh, District Bikaner, shall be released on bail,
if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & [2024:RJ-JD:45158] (5 of 5) [CRLMB-10893/2024] every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 35-himanshu/-
